newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian call money ends flat, gilt yields steady.
newsitem.headline: Indian call money ends flat, gilt yields steady.

text.p: Indian call money and gilts ended steady in moderate trade on Tuesday, dealers said.
Call money ended the day in the 5.50-5.75 percent range against the opening 5.50-6.25 percent, they said.
"The market remains stuck in two ranges," a dealer said.

One was the 10.0-11.0 percent range when call money aligned itself on the export refinance rates, he said. Banks can avail refinance from the Reserve Bank of India against their export credit disbursals at 11 percent.
The second range was the 5.0-6.0 percent range when call money aligned itself on treasury bill yields, he said.
Gilt yields remained steady in moderate trade, dealers said. The 13.50 percent 1997 government of India stock was traded at a yield of 13.08 percent against Monday's 13.05 percent.
The 13.50 percent 1998 stock was traded at 13.51 percent against 13.49 percent while the 13.62 percent 1998 stock was traded at 13.50 percent against 13.48 percent, dealers said.
Dealers said trades in commercial paper had picked up. "Three month paper is being placed for top corporates at 13.25-13.50 percent," a dealer said. "But most of the deals are privately placed."
Rates on intercorporate deposits remained steady at 17.0-19.0 percent for top-rated borrowers, dealers said.
